national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar called on Russian President Vladimir Putin at Kremlin today. Indian Ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar and Joint Secretary (ERS) Mayank Singh were also part of the delegation. The two leaders discussed ways to strengthen India-Russia ties and expand cooperation across key sectors. The meeting focused on bilateral trade, economic cooperation, and preparations for upcoming high-level summits. Speaking at the meeting, Dr S Jaishankar highlighted the strong and growing India-Russia partnership, particularly in the areas of economic cooperation, trade and energy. He conveyed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s greetings and handed over a personal message from Mr Modi. Dr Jaishankar said, the two sides held a meeting of the Intergovernmental Commission earlier in the day and described the outcome as positive. He said, ties between India and Russia have grown significantly across several sectors, including trade, energy, fertilizers and nuclear cooperation. The External Affairs Minister also said Prime Minister Narendra Modi looks forward to meeting the Russian President at the SCO Summit in Bishkek and welcoming him to India for the BRICS Summit. He added that the two leaders are expected to hold their annual summit at a mutually convenient time. Dr Jaishankar said the developments reflect a strong picture of cooperation between India and Russia. Speaking during a meeting, Russian President Putin offered to increase fertilizer supplies to India, saying Moscow is taking steps to support Indian farmers and the country’s agricultural sector. He also highlighted the growth in trade between Russia and India this year. The Russian President credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the growing partnership between New Delhi and Moscow. He said, External Affairs Minister’s visit underscores the level of relations that has been established between Russia and India for decades. He said the two countries are cooperating in practically all areas, reflecting the broad and expanding nature of their bilateral partnership. Earlier in the day, External Affairs Minister along with Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov co-chaired a meeting of the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation in Moscow. Speaking at an event, Dr Jaishankar said, the India-Russia partnership has consistently demonstrated resilience and adaptability. He said, even amid a complex international landscape, bilateral engagement has continued to deepen, reflecting the mutual interests and confidence that underpin the partnership. The Minister highlighted key areas that need to be addressed to achieve the 100-billion-dollar bilateral trade target by 2030, including progress on market access, the removal of tariff and non-tariff barriers, strengthening payment mechanisms, and greater business-to-business engagement. During the meeting, the two sides discussed ways to further expand bilateral trade and economic cooperation and reviewed the India-Russia partnership. Dr Jaishankar reached Moscow yesterday on a two-day visit to Russia. During his visit, the External Affairs Minister is also scheduled to meet his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov to exchange views on regional and global issues.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 140 India calls for sustained international finance for land restoration and drought resilience at COP17
national_raw_news.content: India has stressed the need for diversified, adequate, predictable and sustained international financing to support land restoration and strengthen resilience to drought. Union Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav made the remarks while addressing the Ministerial Dialogue on “Innovative Financial Mechanisms for Healthy Land and Drought Resilience” during the 17th session of the Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) at Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia. The Minister highlighted India’s innovative and diversified financing architecture for land restoration and drought resilience. Mr Yadav emphasized the need for sustained investment in land restoration. He said, land restoration is not a cost, but an investment in food, water, biodiversity, livelihoods and long-term resilience. He stressed that addressing desertification, land degradation and drought at scale requires diversified, predictable and sustained sources of finance beyond public budgets, along with stronger public-private partnerships. The Minister highlighted India’s blended green-finance framework, which enables financing for climate-change adaptation, sustainable land use, forestry and agriculture, afforestation and biodiversity conservation. He also highlighted Sovereign Green Bonds as an avenue to mobilise capital for land restoration, drought resilience, sustainable forestry and other environmental and climate priorities. Mr Yadav also highlighted India’s Green Credit Programme, which enables public and private entities to finance restoration of degraded forest land. Credits are issued after five years of restoration and upon achieving at least 40 per cent canopy density, and may be used once for compensatory afforestation, statutory plantation or CSR obligations. He also highlighted India’s compensatory conservation regime, which channels payments received for forest diversion towards compensatory afforestation and ecosystem restoration, while corporate funding is integrated by the environmental regulatory processes. Underscoring the importance of convergence, the Minister said, bringing public and private finance together through mechanisms such as the Green Credit Programme and compensatory afforestation funds, on the same landscape and alongside citizen participation, represents a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society approach. He emphasised that finance must be continuous, verifiable and connected to local communities. He noted that India’s experience demonstrates what committed domestic resources can achieve, but stressed that this cannot substitute for additional, adequate and predictable international finance for restoration and drought resilience. Concluding his address, the Minister reaffirmed India’s commitment to sharing its experience, safeguards, institutional arrangements, lessons learned and areas requiring course correction.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 269 India to introduce new rules soon for ease of doing business, says Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal
national_raw_news.content: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said India will amend existing regulations and introduce new rules over the next two months to address concerns raised by companies seeking to set up manufacturing operations in the country. Speaking during a programme in Tokyo, Mr Goyal said he met two major corporations earlier in the day–one planning to establish semiconductor equipment manufacturing in India and another operating in the automotive components sector. The minister said he assured them that within the next two months, India will amend its regulations and bring in new rules to accommodate their requests. Mr Goyal said, the government was willing to address issues faced by investors where their demands were fair and justified. On India-Japan economic ties, he said, the two countries were complementary economies, with Japan bringing technology and business practices while India offered a young workforce, scale and a large domestic market. Mr. Goyal added that India and Japan were in active dialogue on working together as trusted partners, including to address concerns around AI being weaponised or monopolised. He also said India’s large domestic market and free trade agreements could provide Japanese companies with opportunities to manufacture in India and access global markets. The minister is leading a nearly 200-business delegation to bolster economic ties between the two nations. The visit will cover Tokyo, Nagoya and Osaka, with representatives from key sectors including manufacturing, semiconductors, clean energy, steel, automobiles, financial services, healthcare and start-ups.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 136 India and China to discuss boundary issues during NSA Ajit Doval’s visit to Beijing
national_raw_news.content: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval arrived in Beijing today on a two-day visit to China. During his visit, Mr Doval will take part in the 25th round of Special Representatives talks between the two countries on the boundary issue with his Chinese counterpart and Foreign Minister Wang Yi scheduled to be held in Beijing tomorrow. Announcing the Special Representatives talks at a media briefing today, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said, Mr Doval and Mr Wang will have an in-depth discussion on the boundary issue as well as other bilateral, regional and international relations. The ties between New Delhi and Beijing came under severe strain after the 2020 Galwan Valley clash and the prolonged military stand-off in eastern Ladakh. But both sides have since taken steps to stabilise relations. Mr Doval and Mr Wang are the designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism, which was established in 2003 to comprehensively address the boundary dispute of the India-China border spanning over three thousand four hundred kilometers. Ahead of Special Representatives talks in Beijing, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday reiterated that peace and tranquillity along the border areas are a prerequisite for good relations with China. During his visit, the National Security Advisor will call on China’s Vice President Han Zheng.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 411 9th National Security Strategies Conference begins in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has directed all agencies to take strict measures against infiltration. Inaugurating the 9th National Security Strategies Conference-2026 in New Delhi today, Mr. Shah directed that an AI-based analysis of information available on Multi-Agency Centre (MAC) platforms should be done to create SOPs to counter various national security challenges. To effectively tackle terrorism and radicalisation, Mr. Shah emphasised training for implementation of the Home Ministry’s PRAHAAR scheme, expediting trials by bringing back fugitives and utilising trial in absentia provisions, and undertaking a comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating UAPA cases. On the first day of the Conference, discussions focused on critical aspects of national security,including response to counter-terrorism challenges, fusion, analysis, and operationalisation of intelligence through the Multi-Agency Centre (MAC), a vision document on narcotics control, detection and deportation of illegal migrants, a policy framework to combat cybercrime, and proxy warfare by Pakistan. Prior to the inauguration, Mr Shah paid homage at the Martyrs’ Column by laying a wreath in remembrance of the brave personnel of the Intelligence Bureau who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty to safeguard national security and integrity. The two-day conference is being held in a hybrid format and is being attended by over 850 participants from across the country. Ministers of State for Home Affairs, Union Home Secretary, Deputy National Security Advisors, Heads of Central Armed Police Forces, and Central Police Organisations attended the conference in Delhi. DGsP of States and UTs, young police officers working at the cutting-edge level, and domain experts from specialised fields joined the conference through virtual mode. The second day of the Conference tomorrow will focus on the threat landscape from sub-aerial systems and formulating countermeasures, securing the blue economy, information warfare and its implications on national security, and the need for a biosecurity framework. Pursuant to the directions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the conference is being held every year in a hybrid format since 2021, with the objective of finding solutions to major national security challenges using the extensive experience of cutting-edge officers working at the grassroots level in collaboration with domain experts.

national_raw_news.title: ‘Khelo India Samvad – Khel Ki Baat PM Ke Saath’ aims to connect youth with vision of national sports 7 mins ago 2
national_raw_news.content: The Union Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports is organising ‘Khelo India Samvad – Khel Ki Baat PM Ke Saath’ in two colleges in every district of Punjab and Haryana and the Union Territory of Chandigarh on August 27 with an aim to connect youth with the national vision of sports, fitness and youth-led nation building. The Samvad will be organized by Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) of the Department of Youth Affairs of the Ministry. Sharing details during a press conference in Chandigarh, today, State Director, MY Bharat Punjab, Rashmeet Kaur informed that students and youth will join the nationally synchronised programme from these venues and listen to the virtual address of Prime Minister, Narendra Modi. This will be followed by local-level interaction with youth and other activities. Officials of Mera Yuva Bharat from Chandigarh and Haryana also addressed the media. Local sportspersons and public representatives will also participate, providing youth an opportunity to share their ideas, suggestions and aspirations. During the programme, youth will also be encouraged to register on the MY Bharat portal and will have the opportunity to submit their suggestions digitally through the MY Bharat Suggestions Box. The Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) 2027 Quiz will also be promoted among the participants.

national_raw_news.title: Men’s Cricket: India declare first innings at 503/9 against Sri Lanka 2 hours ago 39
national_raw_news.content: In Men’s Cricket, Centuries by Dhruv Jurel and Devdutt Padikkal powered India to a hefty 503 for nine declared in their first innings against hosts Sri Lanka on a rain-disrupted second day of the second and final Test in Colombo. In reply, Sri Lanka were reduced to 8 for two at Stumps after pacer Prasidh Krishna and Manav Suthar gave marching orders to Lahiru Udara and Prabath Jayasuriya. For the visitors, Dhruv Jurel produced a flawless display of risk-free batting to score unbeaten 115. Devdutt Padikkal had provided the foundation with a commanding 117 yesterday. With the series already tilted 1-0 in India’s favour, the visitors have strengthened their position with a commanding total. Heavy rain brought an early end to the second session on day two’s play. High winds and darkening skies forced the umpires to halt play, leading to an early tea break. Earlier, India’s star batter Rishabh Pant shattered former skipper MS Dhoni’s record for most Test runs scored by an Indian wicketkeeper away from home. Pant scored a stroke-filled 63 to go past Dhoni. Pant has now scored 2534 runs as wicketkeeper away from home in Test cricket surpassing Dhoni’s 2,496 runs. The list is led by former Pakistan captain Sarfaraz Ahmed, who made 2696 runs away from home in 52 Tests. Australia legend Adam Gilchrist is second with 2634 runs in 41 Tests away from home or at neutral venues.

national_raw_news.title: Chemical sector aims to touch one trillion-dollar vision by 2040, says Union Minister J P Nadda 28 mins ago 19
national_raw_news.content: Chemicals and Fertilisers Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda has emphasised that the Chemical sector has to touch one trillion-dollar vision by 2040 in the country. Addressing a high-level CEO Roundtable today in New Delhi, Mr Nadda said, the Government is committed to establishing a continuous and institutionalised dialogue mechanism with industry, with the objective of identifying impediments and translating suggestions into time-bound action. He said, It will require sustained investment, technology development, stronger domestic manufacturing capabilities. The Minister stated that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Government continues to focus on creating an enabling ecosystem for investment, innovation, sustainability and long-term growth. He also assured that issues raised by the industry are duly noted and shall be suitably taken up relevant stakeholder Ministries. In her address, Minister of State of Chemicals and Fertilizers Anupriya Patel mentioned that Government has brought many reforms and launched schemes to promote manufacturing across the sectors including Chemical and Petrochemical sector such as Bhavya Rasayan, Coal Gasification, Rare Earth Corridors, Critical Mineral Mission, reforms including Tax reforms, Labour reforms. She assured that industry that the Government is committed to transition from a regulatory facilitator to an active growth partner, reducing administrative burden and ensuring the long-term viability of investments. Stressing the importance of government and industry partnership, Secretary Chemicals and Petrochemicals Tejveer Singh stated that the Chemicals sector offers major opportunities across given the expanding domestic demand across key downstream sectors. He emphasized the Department’s commitment to collaborating closely with industry leaders to shape future policy interventions. Speaking on the occasion, MD and CEO, Invest India Nivruti Rai, mentioned that India is well positioned to emerge as a preferred global destination for chemicals manufacturing, supported by its large domestic market, skilled talent, improving infrastructure and ongoing reforms.

national_raw_news.title: ISMA says, sugar prices likely to cool off as sufficient stock available 52 mins ago 37
national_raw_news.content: Indian Sugar and Bio-energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) Director General Deepak Ballani today said, sugar prices are likely to cool off as panic and speculative buying ease, with sufficient stocks available in the country. He said, the rise in sugar prices over the past 20 days was driven by speculative and panic buying. Mr Ballani was talking to a news agency on the sidelines of the ISMA Press Conference in National Capital. He asserted that there are absolutely no problems with sugar availability in the country. On ethanol, Mr Ballani rejected suggestions that diversion of sugar towards ethanol was responsible for the recent price increase adding that domestic consumption remains the first priority. ISMA President Niraj Shirgaokar said the association has sought a reduction in the sugar holding limit for traders from 400 tonnes to 200 tonnes so that more stocks are released into the retail market. He said the government has taken several measures over the past four to six months, including physical verification of stocks at sugar mills and limits on traders, institutional buyers and bulk consumers. Mr Shirgaokar said the government has announced imports of 10 lakh tonnes of sugar as a precautionary measure to ensure comfortable availability.
